tracking.objective: Build a complete, playable 2D run-and-gun arcade game inspired by classic Contra mechanics with original characters, enemies, environments, assets, sound, and boss battles.
requirements: Run-and-gun combat mechanics (8-way aiming, jump shooting, crouch shooting)
Multi-tier weapon pickup & upgrade system (Pulse Rifle, Spread Blaster, Rapid Cannon, Plasma Beam, Rocket Launcher)
Multi-segment side-scrolling level with parallax background layers
Dynamic enemy spawner and wave combat arena locks
Multi-phase boss fight (Jungle Siege Walker) with animated body parts and visual health bar
Heads-Up Display (HP, lives, score, combo counters, weapon status)
Web Audio synthesizer system with custom sound effects and chiptune music tracks
Clean TypeScript compilation and production build
locked: Original game IP and non-infringing assets (no copyrighted Contra sprites/names)
Core game config (WIDTH: 640, HEIGHT: 360, 2x scale, GRAVITY: 1200)
approved: BossHealthBar component with phase indicators and flash tweens
Procedural retro pixel art textures generated in PreloadScene
Procedural Web Audio synthesizer in AudioManager

completed.title: Player physics body crash fix (uncaught TypeError on level start)
completed.description: Player extended Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Sprite but was never registered with the scene's physics system, so this.body was null when the constructor called body.setSize(...), throwing 'Cannot read properties of null (reading setSize)' on every level load. Added scene.add.existing(this) and scene.physics.add.existing(this) immediately after super() in Player.ts, matching the working pattern already used in Enemy.ts. Removed the now-redundant duplicate this.add.existing(this.player) call in LevelOneScene.createPlayer().

completed.title: Bullet-destroy mid-collision-pass crash fix (isParent TypeError)
completed.description: Destroying a bullet synchronously inside the bulletGroup-vs-enemyGroup overlap callback left a stale reference in the group; a later, no-op overlap (bulletGroup vs platforms, no callback) or a second overlapping enemy pair in the same physics step could then touch the already-destroyed body, crashing World.collideObjects with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isParent')". Removed the dead bulletGroup-vs-platforms overlap in setupCollisions(). Hardened handlePlayerBulletHit() to bail out if the bullet's body is already gone, call bullet.disableBody(true, true) to deactivate it immediately, and defer the actual bullet.destroy() to the next tick via this.time.delayedCall(0, ...).

completed.title: Moving platform / elevator undefined-collider crash fix (root cause of persistent isParent TypeError)
completed.description: createMovingPlatforms() and createElevators() called this.physics.add.existing(sprite), which returns the GameObject itself (not a Body), then incorrectly cast the result to Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body and read a nonexistent '.gameObject' property off it. That evaluated to undefined and was passed directly into this.physics.add.collider(this.player, undefined) three times (2 moving platforms + 1 elevator) on every level load. An individual, non-group collider with an undefined target crashes World.collideObjects on the very first physics step -- this was the actual root cause of the isParent TypeError persisting after ACT-018, since it fires during scene setup regardless of bullets or enemies. Fixed by using the returned Sprite directly as the tween target and collider argument, and added setAllowGravity(false) / setImmovable(true) to each platform's body so they behave as proper moving platforms instead of falling under gravity or getting pushed by the player.

completed.title: Platform stale-collision-body fix (player stuck at platform edge)
completed.description: In createPlatforms(), each platform segment sprite was resized from the 'platform' texture's native 160x36 down to a visible 32x36 via setDisplaySize(32, 36), but refreshBody() was never called afterward. For a static-group body, Arcade Physics keeps the collider at the texture's native size until refreshBody() runs, so every 32-wide visible segment actually had a 160-wide invisible collider. Since segments are placed only 32px apart, each one's true hitbox overlapped 3-4 neighboring segments, producing an invisible wall/ledge that trapped the player at certain platform edges. Fixed by calling platform.refreshBody() immediately after setDisplaySize() so the physics body matches the visible sprite. Also audited the full bullet-direction pipeline (InputManager.getAimDirection, Player.handleShooting, BaseWeapon.spawnProjectile, and all five weapon classes) for the reported wrong-direction bullet bug; all already compute velocity from a normalized aim vector with no flipX/stale-pooled-velocity/sign issues, so no changes were needed there.

completed.title: Phase 11 safety pass -- Enemy.die() double/broken scoring fix
completed.description: Enemy.die() called gameState.addScore(this.config.scoreValue * gameState.getPlayerStats().score > 0 ? 1 : 1) -- both ternary branches evaluated to 1, so config.scoreValue was discarded and every kill silently added a flat +1 on top of the correct, combo-weighted score already awarded by LevelOneScene.handlePlayerBulletHit() via player.addScore(enemy.getScoreValue()). Removed the redundant/broken call from Enemy.die(); scoring now only happens once, correctly.

completed.title: Phase 11 safety pass -- PauseMenu dead-button fix (RESTART CHECKPOINT / MAIN MENU)
completed.description: PauseMenu.restartCheckpoint() and mainMenu() both emitted Events.LEVEL_START, which nothing in the codebase ever listened for (LevelOneScene.setupEventListeners() intentionally omits a LEVEL_START handler to avoid a self-restart loop, per its own comment) -- so both pause-menu options were silently non-functional. Replaced both with direct this.scene.scene.start(...) calls, matching the pattern already used by MainMenuScene/GameOverScene/VictoryScene (ACT-013).

completed.title: Full instruction-doc pass (game instructions/01-10) -- boss post-death attack guard
completed.description: Cross-checked the actual implementation against all 10 docs in D:/projects/contra/game instructions/. Doc 07 (Boss Flow) states the boss should never continue attacking after death, but BaseBoss.die() never cancelled in-flight attacks: JungleSiegeWalker.machineGunBurst() (up to 14 shots, 100ms apart), fireMissiles() (3 shots, 200ms apart), and groundStomp()'s hazard spawn were all scheduled via scene.time.delayedCall() with no isDead check, so a boss that died mid-burst could still land hits during/after its own death explosion. Added an isDead guard at the top of each delayed callback.

completed.title: Full instruction-doc pass -- LevelOneScene shutdown cleanup was dead code
completed.description: Doc 10 (Runtime Safety) requires listeners/timers/colliders to be torn down on scene shutdown. LevelOneScene already had a destroy(fromScene) method doing exactly that (HUD/bossHealthBar/pauseMenu/effectsManager destroy + EventBus.removeAllListeners), but a plain method named destroy() on a Phaser.Scene subclass is never invoked automatically -- Phaser tears down scenes via its own event emitter, not by calling an instance method of that name -- so it silently never ran. Wired it up with this.events.once(Phaser.Scenes.Events.SHUTDOWN, this.destroy, this) in create().

completed.title: GameFlowManager per doc 09, added additively
completed.description: Created src/core/GameFlowManager.ts implementing the exact GameFlowState enum + changeState/pause/resume API from doc 09. Wired into LevelOneScene at every transition point the doc lists: intro completion -> PLAYING, ARENA_LOCK/UNLOCK -> COMBAT/PLAYING, checkpoint reached -> brief CHECKPOINT state, PAUSE_TOGGLE -> pause()/resume(), PLAYER_DEATH -> PLAYER_DEAD (restored to BOSS_FIGHT or PLAYING on respawn), spawnBoss() -> BOSS_INTRO then BOSS_FIGHT after 500ms, GAME_OVER/GAME_VICTORY -> matching states. Deliberately additive: existing gameplay gating (isArenaLocked, enemy AI distance checks, EventBus-driven encounter/boss logic) is untouched and still runs exactly as before -- nothing currently switches on GameFlowState the way doc 01's example update() loop does, since rewiring every gate through it blind (no build/test loop) would risk regressing systems that already work. The manager now tracks state correctly and emits GAME_FLOW_STATE_ENTER/EXIT for any future system to consume.

completed.title: PauseMenu CONTROLS self-destruct fix
completed.description: User reported CONTROLS not working even after ACT-026's sibling scrollFactor fix. Root cause: showControls() created the text then registered this.scene.input.keyboard.once('keydown-ENTER'/'keydown-ESC', () => text.destroy()) from inside the handler that ENTER itself had just fired. Phaser's keyboard plugin fires a Key object's own 'down' event before its generic 'keydown-<CODE>' event for the same physical keypress, so the freshly-registered once-listener fired again within that same keypress's processing pass and destroyed the text before it was ever visibly rendered. Replaced with the same controlsVisible state-flag pattern already used for SETTINGS (checked by the persistent top-level enter/esc handlers in setupMenu(), not a listener registered mid-keypress).

completed.title: Bullets falling straight to the ground on fire -- Arcade Group.add() defaults bug
completed.description: User reported fired bullets just dropped to the ground instead of flying. Root cause, confirmed against node_modules/phaser/src/physics/arcade/PhysicsGroup.js: BaseWeapon.spawnProjectile() correctly set each bullet's velocity and allowGravity(false) on its own physics.add.sprite() body, but that body was created outside bulletGroup/enemyBulletGroup and only added to them afterward via the PROJECTILE_FIRED/ENEMY_PROJECTILE_FIRED EventBus listeners. Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Group.createCallbackHandler runs on every member 'added or created' (not just created) and unconditionally re-applies the group's `defaults` to that body -- and since both groups were created via this.physics.add.group() with no config, those defaults were Phaser's stock allowGravity:true and velocityX/velocityY:0. So the instant a bullet was added to its group, its real velocity was zeroed and gravity re-enabled, and it simply fell straight down from the muzzle. Fixed by creating both groups with { allowGravity: false }, and capturing+restoring each bullet's velocity around the .add() call in both listeners (velocity can't be fixed via group config since it varies per bullet).
